newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Interview-HK Bank sees future in personal banking.
newsitem.headline: Interview-HK Bank sees future in personal banking.

text.p: Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp sees personal banking as the key to growth within its Asian boundaries, the bank's international general manager Andrew Dixon said in an interview on Wednesday.
Dixon, who is responsible for the Asian region outside China, also said he expected growth in new technology banking to go hand-in-hand with opening new branches.
"We certainly see, as an institution, that the personal banking area has the greatest potential for long-term relationships," Dixon said.
"We are successful at it in other parts of the world and we intend to increase our coverage of personal banking, certainly in all the countries where I have responsibility," he said.
Dixon said the bank expects to open more branches in the Philippines, Indonesia and India but was in no particular hurry.
"It's not a flood, but as and when the opportunity occurs, if the business plan stands up, we definitely see a connection between bricks and mortar and technology," he said.
In Hong Hong, the bank has 250 branches plus a telephone banking operation.
The HSBC group, for which the bank is the main earnings contributor, also has a "pure" telephone banking operation in Britain in the form of First Direct.
While First Direct was very successful, the Hong KOng telephone banking operation handled more calls.
Hong Kong users of the bank's telephone facilities tended also to be account holders at its branches.

"What that has told us is that there is a definite relationship between convenience and accessibility and the need to build a relationship," he said. "We believe that physical presence leads to other things."

The bank saw Asia as a "huge economic crucible" that was rapidly developing. "Within the region you are seeing a fast developing middle class. You are seeing consumerism appearing where it did not exist 10 years ago," he said.
Dixon was in New Zealand visit the local branch and to address an investment seminar organised by the British consulate in Auckland during Tuesday.
